AAREYDRUGS.technical: Coiling in a multi-month base with a double bottom neckline test near 117. Price holds above rising 21-EMA, 50-SMA, and 200-SMA on 1.63x volume, with RSI at 54. Relative strength is constructive within the base, but overhead supply remains dense.
AAREYDRUGS.fundamental: Operating margins hover around a thin 2-3%, with modest ROCE of 10-12% and negligible leverage. Despite recent bottom-line turnaround, top-line growth of 5.3% fails CANSLIM criteria for institutional sponsorship.
AAREYDRUGS.risk: Fails on a close below 106.41; Minervini discipline mandates immediate exit to prevent structural breakdown back into base lows.

AARTIDRUGS.technical: Developing a classic double bottom pattern, reclaiming all key moving averages including 21-EMA, 50-SMA, and 200-SMA. RSI at 62 confirms constructive momentum without overextension. Neckline pressure at 528 marks the actionable pivot with lower wicks showing absorption.
AARTIDRUGS.fundamental: EBITDA margins expanded 370 bps to 16.6% on strong API and specialty chemical realizations. ROCE sits near 12.9% with manageable debt-to-equity at 0.37x. Turnaround in operational leverage is evident, though two consecutive quarters of 25%+ EPS growth remain pending.
AARTIDRUGS.risk: Stop loss placed at 486.40 below the recent swing low; close underneath invalidates base structure and demands swift loss truncation.

AARTIPHARM.technical: Textbook Stage 2 leader breaking out of a double bottom pivot at 1048.30. Price rides sharply above rising 21-EMA, 50-SMA, and 200-SMA with strong volume expansion. RSI at 71 reflects commanding relative strength and institutional sponsorship without fatal exhaustion.
AARTIPHARM.fundamental: Exemplary CANSLIM fundamentals driven by surging CDMO and xanthine demand. EBITDA surged 84% with margins expanding to 22.2%. Manageable debt profile and robust capacity additions at Atali provide tangible multi-year operational leverage.
AARTIPHARM.risk: Breaching 960.72 pivot low breaks structural Stage 2 support; enforce hard stop immediately to protect capital against sudden reversals.
